question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
Answer: BSP's main competitors for home-services deals are national HVAC/plumbing consolidators, which set add-on pricing, and four sponsor-backed buyers already active in or next to Punctual Pros' PA/NJ counties: Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower) and Northwinds (TruArc). Residential services is the most crowded field on BSP's map (Private-equity landscape).

National consolidators

  • Apex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane and T3/Riverside set add-on pricing (Private-equity landscape).
  • Apex did 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025 (Home-services company case studies).
  • Wrench revenue is est. $1.5–2.0B, a low-confidence figure based on headcount (Competitor filings).

Local PA/NJ rivals

RivalBackerPosition
Sila (King of Prussia)Goldman SachsRevenue est. $450–650M (low confidence); growth almost entirely from acquisitions; bought a training academy in 2026
Legacy/HL BowmanGridiron (Fund V $2.1B)Scaled tier; borrows at par
Ally ServicesWatchtowerBuying in Central PA/NJ
NorthwindsTruArcBuying in or next to the counties
Haller (Lancaster)Owner not in the data254 trucks; healthy rival

(Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings; Home-services company case studies)

Who can actually bid

  • Scaled companies (Wrench, Apex, Redwood, Legacy) borrow at S+425–475, marked at par, with delayed-draw lines for acquisitions (Competitor filings).
  • The next tier has moved to part PIK interest and is marked at 89–94. That tier includes TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber.
  • Horizon has at least $211M of first lien at Blue Owl alone. It pays 3.75% PIK, is marked 92.5, and was lender-owned by 2026.
  • Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.
  • Both Horizon and Heartland are more likely to sell assets or restructure in the next 12 months than to bid for add-ons. That is an inference (est.), not a reported fact.

BSP's position

  • Fund I is about $335M (Form D). Rivals run $0.9–2.1B flagships (Private-equity landscape).
  • The check-size range of $50–250M is unverified (BSP firm profile).
  • The landscape points BSP away from auctions. The suggested focus is:
  • the Authority Brands franchise angle, through territory rights and brand conversion;
  • proprietary outreach to sub-$3M EBITDA shops that large-cap sponsors skip.

Data gaps

The data does not show:

  • current add-on multiples paid in PA/NJ;
  • Haller's ownership;
  • Northwinds' and Ally's deal counts.

Recent closed-deal records and lender filings would answer these questions.

Next actions

  1. Build a proprietary target list of sub-$3M EBITDA HVAC/plumbing shops in Punctual Pros' contiguous counties. Flag targets where Authority Brands territory rights or brand conversion apply.
  2. Track Horizon and Heartland ahead of Dec 15, 2026, for branch or asset sales. Prepare a quick-close process with lenders.
  3. Pull ownership, deal counts and pricing for Haller, Northwinds and Ally to complete the local rival map.
  4. Benchmark Punctual Pros' membership base and technician pipeline against Sila's academy model. This addresses the integration gaps that hurt Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint.
